note: The corpus's first ascending VHDL range, and the design that finds the indexing half of hif-backend#91. `std_logic_vector(0 to 3)` numbers from the left, so a(0) is the leftmost element; hif2verilog used to print the port descending as [3:0] and leave the index alone, so a(0) became a[0] - the least significant bit, which is the other end - and first and last came out swapped. It now prints the port [0:3]. The design reads only the two ends and declares no constant of an ascending type: an ascending-typed literal tripped the other half of #91, where the size was computed as left-right+1 and came out negative, and keeping that out is what made the failure attributable. The oracle is stated as leftmost-bit and rightmost-bit of the driven pattern rather than as a Verilog index, so it holds under either fix - port printed ascending with a[0] kept, or printed descending with the index remapped to a[3].
